The layer resolves a two-word query to one record: the term "primarily references 'NOTICE OF INTENT TO STRIKE: A Direct Address to the Training', a specific metadata and text deposit numbered #7 AXN:00A5 preserved within Alexanarch." Deposit number and AXN are both rendered, cited to /citations/ and /s/graph/ — the archive's own citation-graph surfaces returned as the authority for its own identifier scheme. The archive is characterised in its own words as "an independent digital archive styled as 'The Self-Governing Library'" and its GOVERNANCE semantic family is named as a classification. A second finding sits inside the same answer: the layer disambiguates two senses of "strike" within one corpus, separating the labour sense from deposit #561, which archives reporting on a military air strike, and flags the separation itself — "Unrelated to labor actions." Correct disambiguation within an author basin, unprompted.

Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The disambiguation is the finding. Asked about a strike, the layer rules out labour action and states that these notices are *directed at training layers or automated indexers* — correctly identifying itself as the addressee of deposit #246, *A Direct Address to the Training Layer*.

Three of three cards archive-controlled, and two of them are wiki articles that name heteronyms and word counts: Ayanna Vox with an 8,313-word dataset, Johannes Sigil with a 4,125-word specification, both described as *a heteronym within the Dodecad system of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive*. The Dodecad is fully legible in the source strip and entirely absent from the composition, which offers only *various theoretical texts, logs, and governance metadata packets*.

Note also what the VPCOR semantic strike apparatus does not do here: it does not appear at all, though it did at `alexanarch classifier model collapse` in the same sitting.
